summary: The country dossier located no province-specific trans ordinance, incident series or enforcement finding for this division. Busan and Ulsan are plausibly in the same municipal-obstruction pattern as Daegu (their People Power Party mayors are referenced collectively in the Pride-ban analysis), but the dossier flags that as inference from one sentence, not a scored finding. This division's three sources are national-level: a Seoul court ruling on police restroom advice, an unrestored Yonhap wire, and a national school-restroom survey — none document Ulsan-specific incidents.

sources.summary: Korea Times (22 Jul 2024): Seoul Central District Court ruled that a police officer advising a person in gender transition to avoid public restrooms for a while was a human-rights infringement, awarding 300,000 won of a 3 million won claim; the officer had received NHRCK human-rights education before the suit. National/Seoul-level — no Ulsan content.
NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (navigation shell only; no article body preserved in cache); underlying Yonhap English wire, 8 May 2024, content not verifiable.

Hankyoreh (21 Mar 2024): a youth LGBTQ+ center surveyed 86 trans/genderqueer students — 69% did not feel comfortable using school restrooms, with students describing avoiding drinking to skip urination; a separate Busan study of 208 students found 39% mistreated at school over gender identity or sexual orientation. Advocacy targets the educational-facilities and school-health acts for gender-inclusive facilities. National-level — Ulsan not covered.
